Class SourceScope

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.processing.SourceScope
public final class SourceScope extends Object
The names a generated source file uses, and the imports they need: a GeneratedSources.write(JavaFile, Element...) body gets one to name the types it refers to.

name(...) returns the name to write in the source, and records the import it needs. Types in java.lang and in the generated file's own package need none. A type whose simple name is already taken, by another import or by the generated type itself, is written fully qualified instead.

    • generated

      public String generated()
      Returns the @Generated annotation to put on the generated type, naming the processor. It is empty when javax.annotation.processing.Generated is not visible to the generated code: when the module the code is generated in does not read java.compiler.
      Returns:
      the annotation, such as @Generated("com.example.MapperProcessor"), or an empty string

    • name

      public String name(TypeMirror type)
      Returns the name to write for a type, with its type arguments, recording the imports it needs.
      Parameters:
      type - the type: a primitive type, void, a declared type, an array type, a type variable, a wildcard, or a type javac could not resolve, written as in the source
      Returns:
      the name, such as Map<String, List<Integer>> or Map.Entry<K, V>
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the type is another kind of type, such as an executable or a package type, which has no name; or if it is, or refers to, a local or anonymous class

    • name

      public String name(Class<?> type)
      Returns the name to write for a class, recording the import it needs.
      Parameters:
      type - the class, which may be primitive or an array
      Returns:
      the name, such as List or int[]
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the class has no canonical name, as a local, anonymous or hidden class, or is an array of such a class

    • name

      public String name(String qualifiedName)
      Returns the name to write for a type known by its canonical name, recording the import it needs.
      Parameters:
      qualifiedName - the canonical name, such as java.util.Map.Entry
      Returns:
      the name, such as Map.Entry
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if qualifiedName is not a qualified name: Java identifiers, none of them a keyword, separated by dots

    • name

      public String name(TypeElement type)
      Returns the name to write for a type element, recording the import it needs.
      Parameters:
      type - the type
      Returns:
      the name, such as List or Map.Entry
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the type is local or anonymous, or is nested in such a type: code outside the block that declares it cannot name it
